title: Bring 5 V down to 3.3 V
story: A sensor board runs on 5 V, but the input pin you want to feed only tolerates about 3.3 V. Build a voltage divider with two resistors so the midpoint sits between 3.2 V and 3.4 V. The divider must not waste battery (at most 5 mA) but must not be so weak that any load drags it down (at least 0.5 mA).

goals.label: divider current between 0.5 mA and 5 mA

hints: The output is Vin * R2 / (R1 + R2). You need R2 / (R1 + R2) close to 3.3 / 5 = 0.66, so R2 is roughly twice R1.
Two pairs have the right ratio. The current through both resistors is 5 V / (R1 + R2): use it to choose between them.
